See how this bachelor compares with study options at UCR

This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

VU Public Administration and Organization Science studies how governments, businesses and civil society make decisions, organize people and implement change. The Dutch bachelor combines political and organizational analysis, law, economics, communication and social research. This comparison shows the Besturen route, its open study space and linked team-research and individual-project sequence.

UCR offers three qualified directions: public governance and policy; organizational leadership and responsible decisions; and climate science with public governance. Each has a substantial social-science response to the field, with different priorities. Leadership uses specific ethical and emotion-theory foundations; the climate direction includes substantial scientific and technical study. These do not confer the same disciplinary degree, specialist practicum, independent research sequence or automatic postgraduate eligibility.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Besturen; first-listed route, two selected restricted choices

The Dutch, full-time 2026–2027 bachelor is shown through Besturen, the first officially listed of two equally representative routes; Organiseren is not combined with it. The 24-component pathway contains 60 EC compulsory Year 1 study, 48 EC compulsory Year 2 study and two separate 6 EC restricted choices, then 30 EC open profiling, a 6 EC governance unit, 12 EC team research and a 12 EC individual bachelor project. Beyond Gender Inequalities and AI & Society are the first-listed choices in their respective slots. Qualitative Methods 2 follows participation in Methods 1; quantitative methods follow participation in descriptive/inferential statistics; the research practicum follows participation in quantitative methods. The bachelor project requires at least 90 EC from Years 1–2 and a passed Governance or Consultancy Practicum. It develops an individual academic paper, theoretical/methodological reflection and oral defense from the team-practicum findings. Tutorials are mandatory; group allocation is arranged by the coordinator. The research practicum assesses a group proposal/report and individual professional skills/reflection. Year 3 mentorship must be complete before the bachelor-project grade is awarded. Mentorship in all three years adds no separate EC. The mandatory Dutch diagnostic and any required refresher/remedial course must be passed as part of Academic Skills before that course receives a grade, without extra EC. BSA ordinarily requires 42 EC of first-year courses, subject to exceptions. Practicals and tutorials require attendance. Open choices normally exclude level 100 study and need at least 12 EC at level 300 and board approval; a single 6 EC level 100 prerequisite may be approved within a coherent package. Listed faculty electives and eligible university/listed minors are exempt from prior board approval; the Sociology minor requires an approved replacement for overlap. Internships require prior programme-stage-coordinator approval. Older replaced units and the two route charts are not stacked.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Public Administration and Organization Science at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Public governance, institutions and policy

Combines political institutions, constitutional and European law, public economics, sociology and research methods to examine collective decisions and policy implementation. Organisational behaviour and sustainability governance are present without claiming the VU specialist practicum or thesis.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Organizational leadership, change and responsible decisions

Studies organizational culture, leadership, stakeholder negotiation, digital change and communication through substantive management, social psychology and empirical social methods. Ethical theory and the philosophy of emotion supply explicit foundations for examining responsibility, rationality, motivation and conflict. They are complementary foundations, not workplace consulting methods or a guarantee of merger projects.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Climate science, sustainability and public governance

Asks how public decisions can respond to climate and environmental challenges. Politics, constitutional and European law, public economics, sociology, justice and research methods provide a substantial social-science foundation. Climate, water, biodiversity, circularity, materials and energy courses supply scientific and technical content for evaluating policy options. These domain courses do not reproduce public-management training, organizational consultancy or the VU research sequence.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

The VU route integrates public administration and organizational science with a dedicated methods sequence, Governance Practicum, client-based team research and an individual academic paper and defense. UCR offers substantial related disciplinary study, but does not automatically reproduce that complete professional and research sequence. Literary production, emotion theory and environmental technologies are not substitutes for it.

The climate alternative deliberately combines environmental science and technical options with social, legal, economic and governance study. Its materials, resource and energy courses supply domain knowledge rather than public-management methods. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval; it is not automatically the VU practicum or bachelor project.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Business & Economy in the Age of AI
As we enter the “Age of AI,” this course explores AI’s business, managerial, economic, and societal implications. It is designed for UCR students with a strong interest in AI and requires no prior technical background. The course traces AI’s evolution from early research to generative AI, highlighting its capabilities and limits. Through real-world examples and business cases, students analyse AI’s impact on competitiveness, innovation, labour markets, economic growth, inequality, climate change and society. In this context, students critically examine AI governance and ethics, addressing issues such as bias, privacy, and fairness across business functions (e.g. Marketing, HR, Finance), while also exploring corporate governance and regulation more broadly.
Close

Introduction to Economics
Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
Close

Public Economics
Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
Close

Strategy & Digital Transformation
The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
Close

International Business & Governance
This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
Close

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Personal Leadership
Personal Leadership provides a comprehensive introduction to leadership theory and practice, designed to help students discover their unique leadership style through self-awareness and practical skill-building. Through interactive workshops, reflective exercises, and real-world applications, students engage deeply with core leadership principles and develop the tools needed to lead confidently in any setting.
Close

Leadership Communication
This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.
Close

Leadership & Diversity Management
Leadership & Diversity Management explores how diverse perspectives and experiences shape effective leadership in dynamic, varied environments. Blending cutting-edge theories with hands-on practice, students develop the skills to lead with empathy, inclusivity, and adaptability. Through engaging case studies, interactive workshops, and reflective assessments, participants build awareness of diversity and learn to inspire ethical, collaborative teams.
Close

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.
Close

Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.
Close

Building with Nature
Introduces the sustainable engineering approach of working with natural processes for flood protection, land reclamation and port development. Covers history and principles of ecosystem‑based design, explores case studies and includes guest lectures and field excursions.
Close

Living with Water
Studies water risks and opportunities in deltas, including flood protection, freshwater management, salinisation, subsidence and governance. Readings, discussions and real-world cases examine nature-based adaptation and resilient planning; guest contributions and field activities in Zeeland may be included.
Close

R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
Examines strategies and technologies towards a circular economy. Explores resource security and stewardship, develops lab skills and inorganic chemistry knowledge, and connects to themes at the Delta Climate Center.
Close

Governance of Sustainability
This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
Close

Conservation Biology
Examines human-driven biodiversity loss and approaches to conservation. It studies the causes and effects of extinction risk, current conservation research and projects, and legislation aimed at protecting species and habitats.
Close

Sustainability Essentials I
Introduces sustainability through planetary boundaries: the environmental limits within which human development can take place. It provides foundations for further study in the Environment and Sustainability cluster.
Close

Sustainability Essentials II
Develops physical-science foundations for sustainability through waves, chemistry and materials science. Reflective work and a project apply these topics to analysing greenwashing.
Close

Climate Change
Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society. Discusses adaptation and mitigation solutions, including renewable energy systems, carbon storage and climate‑adaptive planning, and examines climate governance and justice.
Close

Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
Teaches evaluation of environmental impacts of products, processes and services throughout their lifecycle. Emphasises strategic planning for a circular economy through hands‑on learning.
Close

Calling Bullshit
Develops skills to recognise and handle misinformation. Discusses cognitive biases and detection methods, distinguishes real from fake experts, and includes case studies and a video project tackling a misinformation topic.
Close

Renewable System Design
Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy. Explores solar, wind and bioenergy solutions and includes technical and economic analysis; students deliver a report and presentation to a partner company.
Close

Law, Society & Justice
Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students explore legal systems and fields including constitutional, administrative, criminal and international law, human rights and selected private-law topics. Case law and trial simulations support discussion of law, society and justice.
Close

Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
Offers a legal, historical and philosophical approach to human rights. Studies classical and modern philosophers, traces the rise of human rights, examines the US Bill of Rights and the French Declaration, and discusses human rights treaties.
Close

Introduction to Public International Law
Introduction to Public International Law examines the creation and historical development of international law, its sources, subjects and organisation. Topics include the use of force, armed conflict, international criminal law, refugees and environmental law, followed by self-determination, Third World Approaches and treaty politics. Assessment includes exercises, exams, a podcast and reflection.
Close

Comparative Constitutional Law
Comparative Constitutional Law studies constitutional and administrative law through comparison of five legal systems. Students examine how constitutions establish public institutions, define government powers and protect rights and liberties, alongside the relationship between law, democracy and the constitutional state.
Close

Foundations of European Union Law
Introduces the EU legal order. Studies institutions, framework, citizenship and the internal market using problem‑based exercises and guest lectures.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Philosophy of Emotion
Explores emotions from a philosophical perspective. Discusses nature and rationality of emotions, their role in ethics and art, and draws on historical and contemporary sources.
Close

Introduction to Political Philosophy
Introduction to Political Philosophy examines influential Western thinkers from classical antiquity to the present. Students study views of human nature, society and political authority, place theories in their historical settings and compare their arguments and proposed solutions with contemporary political problems.
Close

Foundations of Comparative Politics
Provides analytical tools to compare political systems and democracies. Examines phenomena like democratic backsliding, decline of political parties, rise of populism, media changes, non‑majoritarian institutions and globalization’s impact on domestic politics.
Close

Theory of International Relations
Theory of International Relations introduces schools of thought about international relations and geopolitics. Students apply theories to historical and contemporary cases through readings, group presentations, homework and an exam. A United Nations Security Council simulation asks students to represent a member state in a current international problem.
Close

European Union Politics
European Union Politics examines EU actors, institutions and decision-making rules. Students study how state and non-state interests shape policy and conduct group research on a legislative dossier, interest groups and Members of the European Parliament using the EU transparency register.
Close

Peace & Conflict
Peace & Conflict introduces theories about the causes, consequences and possible resolution of violent and nonviolent conflicts. Historical and contemporary cases address structural inequality, ideology, humiliation and colonial or postcolonial grievances. Students compare international, institutional, cultural and civil-society perspectives and examine how concepts such as justice, truth and reconciliation travel between fields.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Modern Sociology
Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.
Close

Social Movements & Environmental Justice
Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.
Close

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual insights into empirical analysis.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Persuasive Communication
Persuasive Communication builds on classical rhetoric and argumentation to study persuasion in science, society and sustainability. Students examine framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and ethical approaches to persuasion. In a community-engaged project, they help local institutions address communication challenges.
Close

The VU route integrates public administration and organizational science with a dedicated methods sequence, Governance Practicum, client-based team research and an individual academic paper and defense. UCR offers substantial related disciplinary study, but does not automatically reproduce that complete professional and research sequence. Literary production, emotion theory and environmental technologies are not substitutes for it.

The climate alternative deliberately combines environmental science and technical options with social, legal, economic and governance study. Its materials, resource and energy courses supply domain knowledge rather than public-management methods. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval; it is not automatically the VU practicum or bachelor project.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Business & Economy in the Age of AI
As we enter the “Age of AI,” this course explores AI’s business, managerial, economic, and societal implications. It is designed for UCR students with a strong interest in AI and requires no prior technical background. The course traces AI’s evolution from early research to generative AI, highlighting its capabilities and limits. Through real-world examples and business cases, students analyse AI’s impact on competitiveness, innovation, labour markets, economic growth, inequality, climate change and society. In this context, students critically examine AI governance and ethics, addressing issues such as bias, privacy, and fairness across business functions (e.g. Marketing, HR, Finance), while also exploring corporate governance and regulation more broadly.
Close

Introduction to Economics
Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
Close

Public Economics
Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
Close

Strategy & Digital Transformation
The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
Close

International Business & Governance
This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
Close

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Personal Leadership
Personal Leadership provides a comprehensive introduction to leadership theory and practice, designed to help students discover their unique leadership style through self-awareness and practical skill-building. Through interactive workshops, reflective exercises, and real-world applications, students engage deeply with core leadership principles and develop the tools needed to lead confidently in any setting.
Close

Leadership Communication
This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.
Close

Leadership & Diversity Management
Leadership & Diversity Management explores how diverse perspectives and experiences shape effective leadership in dynamic, varied environments. Blending cutting-edge theories with hands-on practice, students develop the skills to lead with empathy, inclusivity, and adaptability. Through engaging case studies, interactive workshops, and reflective assessments, participants build awareness of diversity and learn to inspire ethical, collaborative teams.
Close

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.
Close

Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.
Close

Building with Nature
Introduces the sustainable engineering approach of working with natural processes for flood protection, land reclamation and port development. Covers history and principles of ecosystem‑based design, explores case studies and includes guest lectures and field excursions.
Close

Living with Water
Studies water risks and opportunities in deltas, including flood protection, freshwater management, salinisation, subsidence and governance. Readings, discussions and real-world cases examine nature-based adaptation and resilient planning; guest contributions and field activities in Zeeland may be included.
Close

R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
Examines strategies and technologies towards a circular economy. Explores resource security and stewardship, develops lab skills and inorganic chemistry knowledge, and connects to themes at the Delta Climate Center.
Close

Governance of Sustainability
This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
Close

Conservation Biology
Examines human-driven biodiversity loss and approaches to conservation. It studies the causes and effects of extinction risk, current conservation research and projects, and legislation aimed at protecting species and habitats.
Close

Sustainability Essentials I
Introduces sustainability through planetary boundaries: the environmental limits within which human development can take place. It provides foundations for further study in the Environment and Sustainability cluster.
Close

Sustainability Essentials II
Develops physical-science foundations for sustainability through waves, chemistry and materials science. Reflective work and a project apply these topics to analysing greenwashing.
Close

Climate Change
Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society. Discusses adaptation and mitigation solutions, including renewable energy systems, carbon storage and climate‑adaptive planning, and examines climate governance and justice.
Close

Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
Teaches evaluation of environmental impacts of products, processes and services throughout their lifecycle. Emphasises strategic planning for a circular economy through hands‑on learning.
Close

Calling Bullshit
Develops skills to recognise and handle misinformation. Discusses cognitive biases and detection methods, distinguishes real from fake experts, and includes case studies and a video project tackling a misinformation topic.
Close

Renewable System Design
Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy. Explores solar, wind and bioenergy solutions and includes technical and economic analysis; students deliver a report and presentation to a partner company.
Close

Law, Society & Justice
Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students explore legal systems and fields including constitutional, administrative, criminal and international law, human rights and selected private-law topics. Case law and trial simulations support discussion of law, society and justice.
Close

Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
Offers a legal, historical and philosophical approach to human rights. Studies classical and modern philosophers, traces the rise of human rights, examines the US Bill of Rights and the French Declaration, and discusses human rights treaties.
Close

Introduction to Public International Law
Introduction to Public International Law examines the creation and historical development of international law, its sources, subjects and organisation. Topics include the use of force, armed conflict, international criminal law, refugees and environmental law, followed by self-determination, Third World Approaches and treaty politics. Assessment includes exercises, exams, a podcast and reflection.
Close

Comparative Constitutional Law
Comparative Constitutional Law studies constitutional and administrative law through comparison of five legal systems. Students examine how constitutions establish public institutions, define government powers and protect rights and liberties, alongside the relationship between law, democracy and the constitutional state.
Close

Foundations of European Union Law
Introduces the EU legal order. Studies institutions, framework, citizenship and the internal market using problem‑based exercises and guest lectures.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Philosophy of Emotion
Explores emotions from a philosophical perspective. Discusses nature and rationality of emotions, their role in ethics and art, and draws on historical and contemporary sources.
Close

Introduction to Political Philosophy
Introduction to Political Philosophy examines influential Western thinkers from classical antiquity to the present. Students study views of human nature, society and political authority, place theories in their historical settings and compare their arguments and proposed solutions with contemporary political problems.
Close

Foundations of Comparative Politics
Provides analytical tools to compare political systems and democracies. Examines phenomena like democratic backsliding, decline of political parties, rise of populism, media changes, non‑majoritarian institutions and globalization’s impact on domestic politics.
Close

Theory of International Relations
Theory of International Relations introduces schools of thought about international relations and geopolitics. Students apply theories to historical and contemporary cases through readings, group presentations, homework and an exam. A United Nations Security Council simulation asks students to represent a member state in a current international problem.
Close

European Union Politics
European Union Politics examines EU actors, institutions and decision-making rules. Students study how state and non-state interests shape policy and conduct group research on a legislative dossier, interest groups and Members of the European Parliament using the EU transparency register.
Close

Peace & Conflict
Peace & Conflict introduces theories about the causes, consequences and possible resolution of violent and nonviolent conflicts. Historical and contemporary cases address structural inequality, ideology, humiliation and colonial or postcolonial grievances. Students compare international, institutional, cultural and civil-society perspectives and examine how concepts such as justice, truth and reconciliation travel between fields.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Modern Sociology
Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.
Close

Social Movements & Environmental Justice
Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.
Close

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual insights into empirical analysis.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Persuasive Communication
Persuasive Communication builds on classical rhetoric and argumentation to study persuasion in science, society and sustainability. Students examine framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and ethical approaches to persuasion. In a community-engaged project, they help local institutions address communication challenges.
Close
